title: Parallelism
description: Master parallelism for Grade 11: parallel form in lists, comparisons and correlative conjunctions, and how to fix faulty parallelism — bilingual notes, practice and tests.

topics.title: Parallelism in Lists & Comparisons
topics.concept:
In a list, every item must share the same form — all nouns, all gerunds, all infinitives, or all clauses.

  • ✓ He enjoys hiking, swimming, and cycling. (all gerunds)
  • ✗ He enjoys hiking, swimming, and to cycle. (mixed)
  • ✓ The course is useful, affordable, and short. (all adjectives)

In a comparison, both sides must match in form:

  • ✓ Walking is healthier than driving. (gerund vs gerund)
  • ✗ To walk is healthier than driving. (infinitive vs gerund)

Repeat a marker (to, the, a, that) before each item if it improves clarity: She wants to study, to travel, and to work.

examples.problem: Fix the list: She is intelligent, kind, and works hard.
examples.solution: She is intelligent, kind, and hardworking. — keep all adjectives.

examples.problem: Fix the comparison: Reading is better than to watch TV.
examples.solution: Reading is better than watching TV. — match gerund to gerund.

recap: Every item in a list must share the same grammatical form
Both sides of a comparison must match in form
Repeat a marker (to/the/that) before each item for clarity

topics.title: Parallelism with Correlatives & Faulty Parallelism
topics.concept:
Correlative conjunctions come in pairs and demand parallel structures after each part:

PairParallel example
not only … but alsonot only sang but also danced
either … oreither by bus or by train
neither … norneither here nor there
both … andboth clever and kind

Faulty parallelism is the error of mixing forms. To fix it, find the items, pick one form, and make them all match.

  • ✗ He likes to swim and running. → ✓ He likes swimming and running (or to swim and to run).
  • ✗ Not only she is clever but also kind. → ✓ She is not only clever but also kind.

examples.problem: Fix the correlative: He not only plays the guitar but also the drums.
examples.solution: He plays not only the guitar but also the drums. — balance the two nouns after the pair.

examples.problem: Fix: The task requires patience, skill, and being careful.
examples.solution: The task requires patience, skill, and care. — keep all nouns.

recap: Correlative pairs (not only…but also) need parallel structures
Faulty parallelism mixes forms — pick one and match all
Place the correlative so both items are balanced

questions.q: Which list is parallel?
Fix: 'He is rich, famous, and has power.'
Parallel comparison: 'To give is better than ___.'
Which is faulty?
options: We came to learn and growing.

questions.q: Correlative: 'It is both cheap ___ reliable.'
Fix: 'The job needs skill, effort, and being patient.'
Which keeps parallel form?
options: I like to read, to write, and painting.
I like to read, to write, and to paint.
I like reading, to write, painting.
I like read, writing, to paint.

questions.q: Fix the correlative: 'Either you apologise or leaving.'
options: Either you apologise or you leave.

questions.q: Which list of adjectives is parallel?
Parallel: 'She came to study, to relax, and ___.'
Fix: 'He not only lost the match but also his temper.'
options: He lost not only the match but also his temper.
Not only he lost the match but his temper.
He lost the match not only but his temper.
He not only the match lost but his temper.
questions.explanation: Place 'not only' before the first noun phrase.

questions.q: Which is parallel?
Choose the fully parallel sentence.
options: The committee will review applications, conduct interviews, and selecting candidates.
The committee will review applications, conduct interviews, and select candidates.
The committee will reviewing, interview, and select.
The committee will review, to interview, and selecting.
questions.explanation: All base verbs after 'will': review, conduct, select.

questions.q: Fix the faulty parallelism: 'She is admired for her intelligence, her kindness, and because she works hard.'
options: …for her intelligence, kindness, and hard work.
questions.explanation: Match three noun phrases: intelligence, kindness, hard work.

questions.q: Which comparison is parallel?
options: His goal was to win rather than competing fairly.
His goal was winning rather than to compete fairly.
His goal was to win rather than to compete fairly.
His goal was win rather than competing.

questions.q: Spot the parallelism error: 'The report was clear, concise, and it was persuasive.'
questions.explanation: Drop 'it was' so all three are adjectives.

questions.q: Choose the balanced correlative: 'The scheme benefits ___.'
options: not only farmers but also it helps traders
not only farmers but also traders
farmers not only but traders also
not only farmers but traders helping

questions.q: Which sentence has perfect parallel structure?
options: Reading widely, writing daily, and to think critically improve the mind.
Reading widely, writing daily, and thinking critically improve the mind.
To read widely, writing daily, and thinking critically improve the mind.
Read widely, write daily, and thinking critically improve the mind.

questions.q: Rearrange into a parallel sentence: 'fairly / to / and / firmly / lead / is / to / govern'
options: To lead is to govern fairly and firmly.
To lead fairly is and firmly to govern.
Lead fairly is to govern and firmly.
To govern fairly and to lead firmly is.
questions.explanation: 'To lead is to govern fairly and firmly.' keeps balanced infinitives and adverbs.

questions.q: Which revision best fixes: 'He values honesty, loyalty, and being on time.'
options: honesty, loyal, and being on time
to be honest, loyal, and punctual
questions.explanation: Three parallel nouns: honesty, loyalty, punctuality.

outcomes: Define parallelism and why it matters
Keep items in a list grammatically parallel
Use parallel structure with correlative conjunctions

intro.en: Parallelism means using the same grammatical form for items that play the same role — a list of verbs, a list of nouns, a pair of phrases. "She likes swimming, running, and cycling" is parallel; "swimming, running, and to cycle" is not. Parallel structure makes writing balanced, rhythmic and easy to read — and faulty parallelism is a classic exam error.
intro.hi: समानांतरता (parallelism) का अर्थ है समान भूमिका निभाने वाली मदों के लिए एक ही व्याकरणिक रूप का प्रयोग — क्रियाओं की सूची, संज्ञाओं की सूची, या वाक्यांशों का युग्म। "She likes swimming, running, and cycling" समानांतर है; "swimming, running, and to cycle" नहीं। समानांतर संरचना लेखन को संतुलित, लयबद्ध और पठनीय बनाती है — और faulty parallelism एक उत्कृष्ट परीक्षा-त्रुटि है।

real_life.situation:
A job advert demands parallel skills:

Weak: We want someone who is hardworking, honest, and a person of patience.

Strong: We want someone who is hardworking, honest, and patient.
real_life.why: The strong version keeps all three as adjectives. The weak one mixes two adjectives with a noun phrase ('a person of patience'), which jars. Parallelism is the difference between writing that flows and writing that stumbles.

rule_box.formula: Items in the same role → use the same grammatical form
rule_box.example: She likes to read, to write, and to paint. (all infinitives)

quick_test.explanation: 'reading, writing, painting' are all gerunds — parallel.

common_mistakes.wrong: She likes swimming, running, and to cycle.
He is honest, brave, and a hard worker.
Not only she sings but also dances.
common_mistakes.right: She not only sings but also dances.
common_mistakes.note: Balance the verbs after the correlative.

common_mistakes.wrong: To err is human; forgiving is divine.
common_mistakes.right: To err is human; to forgive is divine.

reading.passage: A good leader must be decisive, fair, and compassionate. She inspires her team not only by setting goals but also by sharing the work. What matters is planning carefully, communicating clearly, and acting boldly. Leadership is less about giving orders and more about earning trust. To lead is to serve, and to serve is to grow.

questions.q: Find a parallel list of adjectives.
Identify the parallel structure after the correlative.
questions.answer: 'not only by setting goals but also by sharing the work' — two parallel 'by + gerund' phrases.

questions.q: Explain the parallelism in the last sentence.
questions.answer: 'To lead is to serve, and to serve is to grow' — matched infinitive structures, creating balance and rhythm.

writing.prompt: Write five sentences with perfect parallelism: a list of gerunds, a list of adjectives, a list of infinitives, a comparison, and a correlative pair.
writing.example: I enjoy reading, writing, and drawing. She is bright, kind, and calm. We hope to learn, to share, and to grow. Cycling is better than driving. He is both wise and witty.

micro_quiz.q: Fix: 'She is kind, clever, and a hard worker.'
Correlative: 'He is not only ___ but also generous.'

options: He likes to cook and baking.
The plan is to research, developing, and to launch.
The plan is to research, to develop, and to launch.
The plan is researching, develop, and launching.
The plan is research, to develop, launching.
challenge.explanation: All infinitives: to research, to develop, to launch.

challenge.q: Fix the correlative placement: 'She not only is a singer but also a dancer.'
options: She is not only a singer but also a dancer.
Not only she is a singer but a dancer.
She is a singer not only but also a dancer.
She not only a singer is but a dancer also.
challenge.explanation: Place 'not only' so both nouns balance after 'is'.

challenge.q: Which sentence keeps parallel form in a comparison?
options: He prefers to walk rather than driving.
He prefers walking rather than to drive.
He prefers to walk rather than to drive.
He prefers walk rather than driving.
challenge.explanation: Match infinitive to infinitive: 'to walk … to drive'.

revision: Parallelism = same grammatical form for items in the same role
Lists: all nouns, all gerunds, all infinitives, or all clauses
Comparisons: both sides must match in form
Correlatives (not only…but also) demand parallel structures
Fix faulty parallelism by choosing one form and matching all items
